title: Faculty at UC3M · Ramón y Cajal Fellow
short_intro: Speech technology, machine learning, and multimodal digital biomarkers for human health.
about: Laureano Moro-Velazquez is a Faculty and Ramón y Cajal Fellow at Universidad Carlos III de Madrid. His research lies at the intersection of speech and audio processing, machine learning, and digital health. He develops inclusive and privacy-aware speech technologies and multimodal digital biomarkers based on speech, eye movements, handwriting, and gait, with particular emphasis on neurological and neurodegenerative disorders. Before joining UC3M, he was an Assistant Research Professor at Johns Hopkins University, at the Center for Language and Speech Processing (CLSP). He has served as principal investigator, co-principal investigator, and co-investigator on projects supported by organizations including NSF, NIH, IARPA, and Amazon, is Associate Editor of the IEEE Transactions of Language and Speech Processing, and has extensive experience teaching and mentoring students across engineering, speech technology, and AI for medicine.

research_themes.title: Speech and health

research_themes.title: Multimodal biomarkers

research_themes.title: Responsible speech AI
